answer: Sybil cost here comes from three stacked mechanisms: one answer per epoch per address, a rotating seed drawn from the shared beacon so answers cannot be pre-computed or replayed, and a seven-grader panel that settles only on four aligned seals. A puppet farm pays full writing cost per identity, gains nothing by copying, and its duplicates fail on merit before payout. Marks carved in cedar on a wharf ledger are cheap to inspect, yet each still needs the lotus seal of independent graders, so faking volume costs more than answering honestly.
